chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Elgar as father figure and teacher
summary: Elgar came to Chicago in 1902, was a founder of the black union, and Saunders first knew him when he visited the Milwaukee boarding school; he became his closest thing to a father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And then he was -- he meant so much to this city, because he come here in 1902, he told me. And -- I mean, around that time. But when he -- he was one of the first ones to start a black union. He was one of the charter members of the union that started. And he was very active and very popular part of the musicians. And he was a good musician and he played good fiddle.

And he was really -- not instrumental, but very -- influenced me so much because he worked at the Wisconsin Roof in Milwaukee, and I was going to this boarding school at that time, and he came -- would come over to mass at our church. And so he got to know everybody, and then with his band he came in and he directed the band and gave it some instructions and all of that. And he picked up the trumpet. It was a cornet then.
But I've never heard such a beautiful tone on a horn. He had a beautiful horn, but the violin was his main instrument. But he was just -- well, he was a professor of music.
You said you were very close to him. Do you remember any particular wise advice he gave you over the years?

Well, he was just like a father down through the years with me. Because I used to call him regularly, and then I'd go over and visit with him, and any time I was playing someplace he would want to come, and he would come to catch us and all of that.

And he gave me the fatherly advice, the do's and the don't because my father -- I didn't know a father, because when I was -- my father deserted us when I was six years old in Memphis, and he left, and I really didn't know a father after that. But one of the closest things to a father to me was Mr. Elgar.
Yeah, and I have a tape that we taped on him, and I have tapes on him.
